formation.title: The League of the Rhine
formation.text:
The princes have gathered at Frankfurt, in the city where the kings of the Germans were chosen, and the lands between the Rhine and the Inn now answer to one league. We stand outside the Holy Roman Empire, and the Empire will not have us: the electors' faith is not ours.

What kind of league this is remains ours to decide. A league of princes in the old manner, each lord keeping his own liberties and the league its many friends; or a sovereign state in the manner of 1806, its ministers reforming, its contingents drilled, its crown answering to no one.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Remain a league of princes within the Reich

modifiers.name: The League of the Princes
modifiers.text: The league keeps the old way of the Rhenish leagues: a compact of princes under the law of the Empire, each keeping his liberties, all keeping the peace together.

options.text: Take our lands out of the Empire, as in 1806

modifiers.name: The Sovereign Confederation
modifiers.text: Sovereign at last: the mediatized counts and knights swallowed whole, conscription and new codes from the ministries at Munich, Stuttgart and Karlsruhe, and a name among the Germans as the princes who broke the Reich.

options.text: A league of free princes, in the old manner

modifiers.name: The League of the Princes
modifiers.text: The league keeps the old way of the Rhenish leagues: a compact of princes under the law of the Empire, each keeping his liberties, all keeping the peace together.

options.text: A sovereign confederation, in the manner of 1806

modifiers.name: The Sovereign Confederation
modifiers.text: Sovereign at last: the mediatized counts and knights swallowed whole, conscription and new codes from the ministries at Munich, Stuttgart and Karlsruhe, and a name among the Germans as the princes who broke the Reich.

advances.name: The Rhenish League
advances.text: In 1254 the cities of the Rhine and the princes beside them swore to keep the King's peace on the river themselves, to raise no unlawful toll and to break the castles of those who did.

event.title: The Rhenish League
event.text:
In the summer of 1254, with the throne of the Empire as good as empty, the citizens of Mainz and Worms swore a league to keep the King's peace themselves. Within months it held some seventy cities from Basel to Cologne and from Aachen to Regensburg, and princes and prelates beside them. Its members swore to raise no unlawful toll on the Rhine and to break the castles of those who did; the robbers of Sooneck and Rheinstein learned what that meant.

The league died three years later over a divided royal election, but it had shown the Rhineland what it could do for itself when no king would.

options.text: The river road is ours to keep

advances.name: The Declaration of Rhens
advances.text: At Rhens on the Rhine in 1338 the electors declared that the king they chose needed no Pope to confirm him. The Rhineland spoke for the Empire, and the Empire listened.

event.title: The Electors at Rhens
event.text:
On 16 July 1338 the electors met in the orchard by the Rhine at Rhens, under the walnut trees where the archbishops of Mainz, Cologne and Trier and the Count Palatine could each ride home before nightfall. There they declared that a King of the Romans chosen by them, or by most of them, needed no confirmation from the Pope to rule.

It was the Rhenish electors speaking for the Empire, and their verdict became the law of the Golden Bull eighteen years later.

options.text: The Rhineland chooses for the Reich

advances.name: The Raft-Masters
advances.text: Fir and oak from the Black Forest, the Neckar and the Main were bound into rafts and floated down the Rhine by the raft-masters' companies, who owned the forests and the rafts alike.

advances.name: The Staple of Cologne
advances.text: From 1259 every cargo passing Cologne had to be unloaded and offered for sale in the city for three days. The Rhine's cities and lords lived by what the river paid them.

advances.name: The Rhenish Gulden
advances.text: In 1386 the four Rhenish electors bound themselves into a monetary union and struck a common gold coin. The Rhenish gulden became the money of account of the whole Empire.

advances.name: The Frankfurt Fair
advances.text: Frankfurt's autumn fair was old in 1240, and in 1330 the Emperor granted it a spring fair as well. Twice a year the merchants of Europe met on the Main.

advances.name: The City League of 1381
advances.text: In 1381 the Rhenish cities joined the Swabian city league against the princes and the knights' societies, and called out their burghers and countrymen to defend their walls.

advances.name: The Electors' Union of Bingen
advances.text: At Bingen in 1424 the electors bound themselves into a union to act together in the affairs of the Empire, whatever the King might want.

advances.name: The Diet of Worms
advances.text: In 1495 the Diet at Worms proclaimed the Eternal Public Peace, which forbade private feuds for ever, and founded the Imperial Chamber Court to judge what the sword could no longer settle.

advances.name: The Wetterau Counts
advances.text: The counts of the Wetterau, Nassau, Solms, Isenburg, Hanau and their neighbours, too small to stand alone, joined their voices into one collective vote in the Diet and their houses into one union.

advances.name: The Frankfurt Book Fair
advances.text: Within a generation of Gutenberg's press at Mainz, the printers and booksellers of Europe came to the Frankfurt fair to buy and sell. For a century and a half it was the book market of the Western world.

advances.name: The Protestation of Speyer
advances.text: In 1529 six princes and fourteen cities protested at the Diet of Speyer that in matters of conscience no majority could bind them.

event.title: The Protestation of Speyer
event.text:
On 19 April 1529 the Diet at Speyer revoked the tolerance it had granted three years before and set the Edict of Worms against Luther back in force. Six princes and fourteen imperial cities refused: in matters of God's honour and the salvation of souls, they said, each must stand before God alone. From their protest the new faith took its name.

The Rhenish and Hessian princes stood on both sides of that day. Which side does ours stand on?

options.text: We stand with the protesting estates

modifiers.name: The Protesting Estates
modifiers.text: We stood with the princes and cities who protested at Speyer that no Diet may bind a conscience.

options.text: The Edict of Worms is the law of the Reich

modifiers.name: The Edict of Worms Upheld
modifiers.text: We held to the law the Diet of Worms had made against Luther, and the old Church holds to us.

advances.name: The Frankfurt Exchange
advances.text: In 1585 the merchants at the Frankfurt fair agreed on one set of exchange rates for the hundred coinages of the Empire, and the Frankfurt exchange was born.

advances.name: The Landesdefension
advances.text: Around 1600 Landgrave Maurice of Hesse-Kassel, John of Nassau and the Elector Palatine drilled the countrymen of their lands into a defending militia on the Dutch model.

advances.name: The War School of Siegen
advances.text: In 1616 Count John VII of Nassau-Siegen opened a school at Siegen to teach young nobles the art of war from books and drill: the first military academy in Europe.

advances.name: The Protestant Union
advances.text: At Auhausen in 1608 the Elector Palatine, Baden, Wuerttemberg, Ansbach and the imperial cities joined in a union for mutual defence, and each member kept a quota of soldiers ready.

advances.name: The Rhenish Alliance
advances.text: In 1658 the Elector of Mainz led the Rhenish princes into an alliance to guard the peace of Westphalia, with the Kings of France and Sweden as partners. For ten years it held the balance of the Empire.

event.title: The Rhenish Alliance
event.text:
On 14 August 1658, at Frankfurt, while the electors crowned Leopold, the Elector of Mainz Johann Philipp von Schönborn closed a league with the archbishops of Cologne and Trier, the Palatinate of Neuburg, Münster, the dukes of Brunswick, Hesse-Kassel and the King of Sweden, with the King of France beside them. Its purpose was the peace of Westphalia: no Spanish troops through the Rhineland, no Emperor making war on his own princes.

Six years later its contingent stood beside Montecuccoli on the Raab and broke the Ottoman army at Saint Gotthard. The Alliance served two masters, Paris and Vienna, and every prince in it had to choose which came first.

options.text: Take Mazarin's subsidies and his guarantee

modifiers.name: The French Guarantee
modifiers.text: Mazarin's subsidies pay the Alliance's soldiers and envoys, and the King of France guarantees the peace of Westphalia beside us.

options.text: The Alliance serves the Emperor's peace

modifiers.name: The Emperor's Peace
modifiers.text: The Alliance's regiments marched to the Raab and stood at Saint Gotthard: the princes keep the Emperor's peace with their own soldiers.

advances.name: The Alliance Contingent
advances.text: In 1664 the Rhenish Alliance sent some six thousand men under Waldeck to the Raab, and they stood in the line at Saint Gotthard when the Ottoman army broke.

advances.name: The Huguenot Colonies
advances.text: After 1685 the Calvinist princes offered the refugees from France land, exemptions and freedom of worship. New towns rose for them at Neu-Isenburg, Friedrichsdorf, Karlshafen and Christian-Erlangen.

advances.name: Dutch Timber
advances.text: The Dutch built Amsterdam on piles and their fleets on German masts. From the later seventeenth century the Black Forest rafts grew to floating villages of several hundred men, bound for Dordrecht.

advances.name: Mediatization
advances.text: Between 1803 and 1806 the bishoprics, abbeys, imperial cities, counts and knights of the south and west were placed under the larger states. A map of hundreds of sovereignties became a map of a few.

event.title: Mediatization
event.text:
The Recess of 1803 gave the prince-bishoprics and abbeys to the secular princes, and the Act of Confederation of 1806 finished the work: the imperial counts, the princes too small to keep their own sovereignty and the imperial knights were placed under the larger states. Hundreds of little sovereignties ended in a few years. The mediatized houses kept their estates, their courts and their rank as Standesherren, and their grievances.

The new lands can be made ours outright, or their lords can be won over.

options.text: One state, one law: absorb the mediatized lands

modifiers.name: The Mediatized Lands Absorbed
modifiers.text: The little sovereignties are gone into the state, their courts closed and their revenues collected by our officials.

options.text: Honour the Standesherren and their courts

modifiers.name: The Standesherren Honoured
modifiers.text: The mediatized houses keep their estates, their patrimonial courts and their rank, and they keep the peace with us.

advances.name: The Federal Contingent
advances.text: The Act of Confederation bound its members to a contingent of 63,000 men: thirty thousand from Bavaria, twelve thousand from Wuerttemberg, eight thousand from Baden, and the rest from the smaller states.

advances.name: The Chevaulegers
advances.text: The light horse of Bavaria and Wuerttemberg were the best cavalry of the Confederation, and rode with the Grande Armée from Wagram to Borodino.

advances.name: Conscription
advances.text: Bavaria introduced conscription in 1805 to fill the ranks the alliance with France demanded; Wuerttemberg and Baden followed.

advances.name: The Rhine Octroi
advances.text: The Octroi convention of 1804 swept away the river's thirty-odd tolls for a single toll, collected by one administration at Mainz. After 1815 the Central Commission for the Navigation of the Rhine carried the work on.

advances.name: The South German Constitutions
advances.text: Bavaria and Baden in 1818 and Wuerttemberg in 1819 gave themselves written constitutions and elected chambers, the first in the German lands.

destiny.name: The Confederation of the Rhine
destiny.text: The princes between the Rhine and the Inn answer to one league. Whether it stays a league of princes in the old manner or becomes the sovereign confederation of 1806 was chosen at its founding; what it makes of that choice is the work of generations. Requires stability of at least 25.

event.title: A Confederation on the Rhine
event.text: The envoys of the princes have taken their lodgings in Frankfurt, and the league has begun to speak with one voice. What it says, and to whom, is now ours to decide.

options.text: Let the league be heard

destiny.name: The Electors of the Rhine
destiny.text: The Electoral Rhenish Circle joined the sees of Cologne and Trier to Mainz and the Palatinate, and every Rhenish league of princes, from Bingen to the Alliance of 1658, began with those electors. Hold Cologne and Trier, ourselves or through princes who answer to us, and gather at least three princes into the league as subjects. The league keeps its members; it does not swallow them.

conditions.text: Chose the League of the Princes destiny
Own Cologne, or a subject owns it
Own Trier, or a subject owns it
At least 3 subjects that are not tributaries (princes of the league)

event.title: The Electors of the Rhine
event.text: Cologne and Trier, the electoral sees on the Rhine, stand with the league, and the princes who joined it keep their own courts and their own laws. The electors who once met at Rhens and Bingen to speak for the Empire now speak for the league.

options.text: The princes keep the peace

destiny.name: The Fair of the Empire
destiny.text: Frankfurt was where the kings of the Germans were chosen and where the Empire came to trade at the spring and autumn fairs. Grow Frankfurt to at least 53 development, half again what it had in 1337, build a Messehof there and hold at least 50 prestige.

conditions.text: Frankfurt is ours and has at least 53 development
Frankfurt is ours and has a Messehof

event.title: The Fair of the Empire
event.text: The fair court at Frankfurt is full from the Easter fair to the autumn one. Merchants from Lyon, Leipzig and Antwerp crowd the Römerberg, and between the stalls the envoys of the princes meet as they never could in the Diet. The question is which crowd the league should serve first.

options.text: The merchants come first

modifiers.name: The Merchants' Fair
modifiers.text: Frankfurt's fair serves the merchants first, and the goods of the Empire go out with them.

options.text: Call the princes' congress

modifiers.name: The Princes' Congress
modifiers.text: The envoys of the league meet at the fair and settle what the Diet never could.

destiny.name: The League of Princes
destiny.text: In 1785 Hanover and Saxony, with Prussia, bound the German princes into a league against the Emperor's plan to trade Bavaria away. Bring Hanover and Dresden into the league, ourselves or through its princes, keep at least six princes as subjects and hold at least 75 prestige.

conditions.text: Own Hanover, or a subject owns it
Own Dresden, or a subject owns it
At least 6 subjects that are not tributaries (princes of the league)

event.title: The League of Princes
event.text: Hanover and Saxony sit in the league beside the Rhenish princes, and the Emperor can no longer trade a German land away without asking all of them. The league of 1785 was a shield; what it shelters is up to us. Some of its princes keep poets at court, others keep fortresses.

options.text: Shelter the courts of the muses

modifiers.name: The Courts of the Muses
modifiers.text: The small courts of the league keep poets, scholars and theatres.

options.text: Arm the league against the Emperor

modifiers.name: The Armed League
modifiers.text: The princes' fortresses stand ready against the Emperor, and the workshops pay for them.

destiny.name: The Franconian Circle
destiny.text: Franconia was the most divided circle of the Empire: prince-bishops at Würzburg and Bamberg, margraves at Ansbach and Bayreuth, the free city of Nuremberg and hundreds of knights. Between 1803 and 1810 nearly all of it went to Bavaria, with the free city of Augsburg beside it. Rule at least nine tenths of Franconia and Augsburg directly, not through subjects, and gather a treasury of at least 1,000 gold.

conditions.text: At least 90% of the locations of Franconia are ours, ruled directly

event.title: The Franconian Circle
event.text: The magistrates of Nuremberg and Augsburg have handed their keys to our commissioners, and the bishops, counts and knights of Franconia have lowered their banners. The lords and cities that answered only to the Emperor now answer to us. Nothing stands between the sovereign and his subjects any more.

options.text: One sovereign, one law

destiny.name: The Peace of Pressburg
destiny.text: At Pressburg in December 1805 Austria gave up the Tyrol and Vorarlberg, and within a week the princes of the south were kings. Rule Innsbruck and Bregenz directly, bring the state toward one centre (the centralization balance at the middle or past it) as Montgelas did in Bavaria, and hold at least 2,000 gold.

conditions.text: Our Centralization vs Decentralization value has come to the middle or past it toward centralization (0 or lower)

event.title: The Peace of Pressburg
event.text: Innsbruck and Bregenz fly our flag, and the old patchwork is gone: one ministry, one tax, one army. The reformers want to finish the work of the state, the generals want an army fit for a kingdom. The treasury can carry only one of them at full speed.

options.text: Give the ministries their way

modifiers.name: The Ministries of Montgelas
modifiers.text: The monasteries secularized, serfdom ended, the schools made compulsory: the state reformed from one centre.

options.text: Build the royal army

modifiers.name: The Royal Army
modifiers.text: A conscripted army drilled for a kingdom; the villages pay for it in men.

destiny.name: The Confederation at Its Height
destiny.text: By 1808 the Confederation reached the Elbe: the Kingdom of Westphalia, made from Brunswick, Hesse-Cassel and Magdeburg, had joined it. Rule Magdeburg and Brunswick directly, hold at least 75 prestige and a treasury of at least 3,000 gold.

event.title: The Confederation at Its Height
event.text: Our writ runs from the Rhine to the Elbe, and Magdeburg and Brunswick send their contingents with the rest. Every crown in the Confederation was won beside a stronger ally. Some say the alliance must be served to the end; others remember that the princes of 1813 changed sides at Ried and kept everything.

options.text: March with the great ally

modifiers.name: The Contingent of the Confederation
modifiers.text: Our horse march with the great ally, drilled in its manner, and the blockade closes the sea to our ports.

options.text: Change sides in time, as at Ried

modifiers.name: The Treaty of Ried
modifiers.text: The crown changed sides in time and kept its lands, its rank and its claims.

units.name: Alliance Regiment
units.text: Infantry of the Rhenish Alliance, raised from the companies of many princes and drilled to stand together, as they stood at Saint Gotthard in 1664.

units.name: Rheinbund Line Infantry
units.text: Line infantry of the federal contingents, drilled on the French model and hardened from Aspern to the Beresina.

units.name: Chevaulegers
units.text: Light horse of Bavaria and Wuerttemberg, quick to the charge and lightly protected.

units.name: League Burgher Militia
units.text: Burghers and countrymen called out by the Rhenish city league to hold the walls and the river road.

units.name: Landesdefension
units.text: The princes' drilled country militia of shot and pike.

units.name: Rheinbund Konskribierte
units.text: Conscripts of the Confederation's states, raised by lot to fill the federal contingent.

buildings.name: League Watch
buildings.text: A post of the Rhenish League's peace on the river road, kept to see that no lord raises an unlawful toll and no robber stops a barge.

buildings.name: Raft Yard
buildings.text: The yard of a raft-masters' company, where felled timber is bound into rafts and floated down to the markets of the Rhine.

where.text: Lumber is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Fair Court
buildings.text: Halls and yards for a twice-yearly fair in the Frankfurt manner, where the merchants of many lands meet to buy, sell and settle accounts.

buildings.name: Imperial Chamber Court
buildings.text: A seat of the court founded at Worms in 1495, where the feud gives way to the lawsuit and the jurists of the Empire sit.

buildings.name: Exchange
buildings.text: An exchange of the Frankfurt kind, where merchants fix the rates of the Empire's many coinages and bills change hands.

buildings.name: War School
buildings.text: A school on the model of Siegen, where officers learn the art of war from books and drill the country's militia.

buildings.name: Huguenot Colony
buildings.text: A settlement of refugees from France under the prince's privilege, with its own church and its own trades.

buildings.name: Octroi Office
buildings.text: An office of the Rhine Octroi, collecting the one toll that replaced the river's many.

list.name: The Mainz Directory
list.text: By the Golden Bull of 1356 the Archbishop of Mainz alone summoned the electors, and as archchancellor of the Empire he led their college and held the formal channel between the Emperor and the estates at the Diet. What the Diet took up passed through his chancery, and the college of cities, voting last, counted for little. Karl Theodor von Dalberg, the last archchancellor, carried the office to Regensburg in 1803 and into the Confederation as its Prince-Primate in 1806.

list.name: The Thurn und Taxis Post
list.text: Rudolf II granted the imperial post its monopoly in 1597, and in 1615 the office of Postmaster General became hereditary in the house of Taxis. The princes set up posts of their own against it, yet the house outlived the Empire: Bavaria and Baden granted it their posts as fiefs in 1806, and from 1810 it was run from Frankfurt for Hesse, Wuerttemberg, the free cities and the small states until Prussia bought it in 1867 for three million thaler.

list.name: The Kriegskasse
list.text: From 1687, when Landgrave Charles lent his regiments to Venice against the Ottomans, Hesse-Kassel hired out its army to the powers at war, and the subsidies went into a military treasury under the prince's own hand, beyond the estates' grant. Between 1702 and 1765 they met a good half of the state's budget. In 1776 Hesse-Kassel leased twelve thousand men to Britain, and Hesse-Hanau, Waldeck, Brunswick and Ansbach-Bayreuth did the same.

list.name: The Standesherren
list.text: The princes and counts placed under the larger states between 1803 and 1815 lost their laws, taxes, appeal courts, police and conscription, but kept their lands, their courts of first instance and their standing as the equals of reigning houses. The Federal Act of 1815 gave them seats in the first chambers of the states that had absorbed them.

list.name: The Rhenish Law
list.text: The French civil code of 1804 stayed in force on the left bank of the Rhine after Napoleon's fall, and the Rhinelanders held to their Rhenish law against Prussia until the German Civil Code replaced it on 1 January 1900. Baden made the code its own Landrecht, in force from 1 January 1810 with more than five hundred additions by Johann Nikolaus Friedrich Brauer.
